title: Per-request fragment checksums and client repair-hints for hosted SSE disconnects
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customer escalations showed that when a hosted SSE connection disconnects mid-response, clients sometimes receive truncated or duplicated output after reconnect/replay. Root cause analysis points to inconsistent fragment attribution under transient proxy buffering + multi-worker handoffs: stream fragments (partial token batches) were being replayed without an authoritative per-request integrity check, which allowed silent reorder/duplication when reconciling on reconnect.

Impact: High for interactive chat customers and streaming SDK users (seen as duplicated tokens, missing suffixes, or final response truncation). Affects hosted API only; Dedicated/Private exposures differ due to their session affinity. Several high-touch customers reported production incidents during peak traffic, increasing support load and SLA risk.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Start a long-generation streaming request via hosted API with SSE.
2) Simulate proxy buffer flush or worker handoff (tcpkill or graceful drain).
3) Reconnect client using resume token and request server-side resume.
4) Observe duplicated token spans or missing suffix when fragments cross boundaries.

Root cause hypothesis:
- No per-request fragment checksum or authoritative fragment sequence embedded in the event stream.
- During handoffs, buffered fragments can be resent by intermediate components without detection.
- Clients rely on resume offsets but cannot detect subtle semantic divergence (e.g., partial token cutoff mid-codepoint).

Proposed design:
1) Attach lightweight per-fragment metadata to SSE events: sequence_number (monotonic per request), fragment_length_bytes, and a 32-bit CRC32 checksum covering the fragment payload. Metadata is transmitted as JSON-encoded SSE 'meta' event preceding or paired with token events.
2) Server maintains ephemeral fragment tombstones (sliding window) for O(30s) so reconcilers can verify whether a requested resume offset maps to an exact fragment or needs backfill.
3) Introduce a client-visible repair hint header/event: X-Stream-Repair-Hint (and SSE event 'repair_hint') that suggests an authoritative resume cursor and backfill length when mismatch detected. This lets SDKs decide to request a backfill or perform a full re-request.
4) Add a circuit-breaker and metric: if >5% of reconnects within a minute require full re-request, auto-sample increased logging and an emergency mitigation.

Backward compatibility / rollout:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag 'stream_fragment_checksums'. Older SDKs will ignore new meta events; we will maintain legacy resume behavior until we enable server-side checks in per-tenant rollout.
- Provide a temporary "best-effort" reconciliation patch that strips duplicate trailing tokens for clients using the SDK shim (short-term mitigation while rollouts progress).

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Design doc + API contract (Confluence) (done)
- Runtime: add fragment metadata producer and checksum calculation (PR #4123) -> staging test (done)
- SDK changes: expose repair_hint and verify fragment checksums on reconnect (PR #4187) -> integration tests pending
- Tombstone store: ephemeral in-memory LRU with tenant-aware limits (PR #4192) -> review
- Canary rollout for 10% of hosted traffic, monitor error-rate and duplication metrics -> data-driven ramp
- Full rollout with feature flag off by default, turn on per-tenant after stability verified

Observability: Add Grafana panels showing: reconnects requiring repair, percent of reconnects that received repair_hint, duplication rate, per-tenant error spikes. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/streaming-error-rate?var-env=prod

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Deployed temporary patch to token trimming pipeline to reduce duplicated trailing tokens for ~3 affected customers (hotfix v1.21.4).
- Support runbook updated with recommended client-side backoff and re-request guidance.

Notes/Trade-offs:
- Adding per-fragment checksums increases event size slightly (~16-24 bytes) and CPU for CRC calculation; expected <1% p99 latency increase on token emission. We measured this on staging and validated within SLA.
- Tombstone retention window is a tuning knob: larger window reduces missed resumes but increases memory. Default 30s tuned for common reconnect patterns.
- We avoid cryptographic hashes to keep CPU low; CRC32 is chosen for speed and collision tolerance for this use case.

Next steps: finish tombstone implementation, merge SDK PR, run canary, and coordinate tenant opt-ins via Console.

updates: 2026-03-06 - Triage: Incident triaged by oncall and SE; classified as high-impact; assigned to Liam. Initial mitigation: token-trim hotfix deployed to affected tenants.
2026-03-07 - Staging: Runtime PR #4123 merged to staging. Verified CRC32 calculation microbench: 0.4% median CPU impact on 8k-token/hr emitter in staging cluster.
2026-03-09 - SDK: Began SDK integration (repair_hint parsing + auto-backfill behavior). Encountered edge-case with multibyte codepoint boundaries; added boundary-safe backfill logic.
2026-03-10 - Canary: Enabled fragment_checksums flag for 10% of hosted traffic. Early signal: reconnects requiring full re-request dropped 62% for sampled tenants.
2026-03-12 - Regression: Observed race during worker handoff where tombstone cleanup raced with verify; introduced per-request lock to avoid false negatives. Patch in PR #4192.
2026-03-14 - Merge: Fix validated in staging; tombstone PR merged. Preparing SDK PR for final review and integration tests. Planning full canary ramp to 30% next week.
